title: Huayan
hookLine: the school of the Flower Garland Sutra

lines: TIANTAI: HE CAME DOWN TO MEET US.
ANOTHER SCHOOL: THAT WAS THE WHOLE.
cards: Two schools, one story. Chinese Buddhists told it like this.
Right after the Buddha woke up under the tree, before he walked anywhere or taught anyone a simple word, he poured out a teaching so vast that the people around him couldn't follow it.
They sat there, the story says, as if they could neither hear nor speak. So he started again, simpler. Tiantai heard that story and said: you see, the Buddha had to come down to meet people.
Another school heard the very same story and said: you see, the first thing out of his mouth was the whole truth. That second school is today's word. Huayan.

teach.h: NAMED FOR A BOOK, NOT A MOUNTAIN.
teach.b: Tiantai was named for a mountain. Huayan is named for a book: Huayan is the Chinese title of the Avatamsaka Sutra, the Flower Garland.
This path spent time inside that sutra earlier this year: Indra's net, the pilgrim Sudhana, the tower where every room holds all the others. Today, the people who made a school of it.

teach.h: A LINE OF MASTERS, AND FAZANG.
teach.b: Huayan remembers a line of masters who handed the teaching on. The one this path has met before is Fazang, the monk who explained the sutra to an empress using a golden lion.
Like Tiantai, Huayan sorted the Buddha's teachings into kinds.
Both schools kept every sutra, and both put one at the summit: for Tiantai, the Lotus; for Huayan, the Flower Garland, which its teachers call the round, or complete, teaching.
Each school has its reasons, and Chinese Buddhists could study both. And the book at Huayan's center isn't a list of rules or a set of arguments. It's a vision.
Light pours from the Buddha, worlds open inside worlds, and everything turns out to be woven into everything else.

teach.h: A VISION TO PUT INTO WORDS.
teach.b: Huayan's teachers set themselves a hard job: to put that vision into words a person could study and practice. Next come two of the ways they tried, interpenetration and a golden lion.
But it starts with a garland: many flowers, strung on one thread, each still its own flower.

how: Huayan Buddhists study the Flower Garland Sutra and the writings of masters such as Fazang, and contemplate the interconnection of all things it describes; the sutra is also studied in Korea and Japan.

o: a garland of flowers offered at a Chinese shrine
the Chinese school built on the Flower Garland Sutra

games.q: the story says the Buddha's first teaching was too vast for anyone to follow. you're a Huayan teacher. what do you make of it?
o: it was a false start, best forgotten.
it was the whole truth, given first.
it was meant only for gods.
games.why: Huayan reads the Flower Garland as the complete teaching. Tiantai, hearing the same story, stresses that the Buddha came down to meet people.

practice: Bring back the picture this path met earlier: a net stretching in every direction, a jewel at every knot, each jewel reflecting all the others.

Don't try to see the whole net; rest on one jewel and let the others show up in it as faint reflections. Then let that jewel be you, sitting here, catching a little light from everyone you met this week.

wordCard.voice: Huayan. The Chinese school built on the Flower Garland Sutra, which its teachers hold as the complete teaching. Today's word.

orig.note: Chinese Huayan: the Chinese title of the Flower Garland (Avatamsaka) Sutra, and of the school.
